review_notes: I read the whole file. I did not open the imported CanonicalDrift and PicardSolution files, so the `.comp` rewrite below was not checked against them. The only real repetition is the measurability argument for the limsup drift, which appears in `measurable_drift` and again inside `decode_integral_equation`. The other lemmas (`drift_mem_Icc`, `drift_response`, `drift_relabel` and so on) are thin unfold-and-apply wrappers around imported API, so I did not report them. The finding is small. findings.excerpt:
apply Measurable.limsup
    intro n
    exact (hf n j).comp hp
findings.problem: The `hm` block in `decode_integral_equation` unfolds `drift` with `change` and re-proves, by `Measurable.limsup` over `n`, that the limsup drift is measurable. `measurable_drift` already proves this on the product space `α × (ℝ × (ι → ℝ))` from the same hypothesis `hf`. The block re-derives that lemma and then specializes it to fixed `a` by composing each `hf n j` with `hp`.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the `hm` proof with a composition of the existing lemma with the section embedding `hp`: `have hm : ∀ j, Measurable (fun p : ℝ × (ι → ℝ) => drift f a p.1 p.2 j) := fun j => (measurable_drift f hf j).comp hp`. `drift f a p.1 p.2 j` is definitionally the composite `(fun q => drift f q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2 j) ∘ (fun p => (a, p))`. Then `change`, `apply Measurable.limsup` and the per-`n` composition are all unnecessary. Both uses then go through one proof of limsup measurability, and `decode_integral_equation` no longer unfolds `drift`.
findings.benefit: The limsup-measurability argument lives in one place, `measurable_drift`. If `drift` is redefined, or `Measurable.limsup` is replaced, only that lemma needs updating. The proof of `decode_integral_equation` shrinks to a one-line composition that states the intent (a section of a jointly measurable map), and it stops depending on the internal form of `drift`.
